title: Disjoint union activation of difference distance magic labelings
summary: A graph is difference distance magic orientable (DDMO) if its vertices can be labeled bijectively by consecutive positive integers and its edges oriented so that the incoming and outgoing neighbor-label sums agree at every vertex. We give an affirmative answer to the disjoint-union question posed by Aceska et al. in January 2026: two copies of the non-DDMO graph K₃,₃ have a DDMO disjoint union. More precisely, for k ≥ 1 and r ≥ 0, the graph consisting of k disjoint copies of K₃,₃ and r isolated vertices is difference distance magic orientable if and only if k is even or r ≥ 1. The proof…
